 Nepal will face host Oman at 11:15 a.m. on Monday, October 19, at Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman, in its final ICC Cricket World Cup League 2 match. According to English Desh Sanchar, Nepal needs a victory to secure a top-six finish and retain its One Day International status without entering the qualifying playoffs.
 The match carries major consequences for Nepal's international standing. A win would place the team among the top six in League 2, securing its ODI status directly. If Nepal fails to achieve that position, it will have to compete in the World Cup Qualifier Playoff to preserve its status.

 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 Nepal enters the decisive fixture after losing to Canada by 24 runs in its previous match, a result that dropped the team to seventh place in the standings. However, English Desh Sanchar reported that Nepal maintains a better net run rate than Canada, which occupies sixth place.

 Nepal Beat Oman by 10 Runs to Regain Sixth Place 
 A point from an abandoned match could still give Nepal a chance to break into the top six, according to the report. With rain considered unlikely in Oman, the Nepali side is targeting a full victory to improve its position.
 Nepal has already beaten Oman by 113 runs in the second match of the current series. The team will seek to reproduce that result in Monday's encounter as it attempts to secure direct retention of its ODI status.
 The head-to-head record between the two teams is evenly balanced. Nepal and Oman have met 12 times in ODI cricket, with each side recording six victories. However, Nepal has won its last three encounters against Oman, giving the visitors a positive recent record ahead of the decisive match.
